title: NVIDIA puts $3.5B into MediaTek to seed its NVLink Fusion custom-chip ecosystem
subtitle: A convertible-bond stake ties MediaTek's custom AI accelerator business to NVIDIA's interconnect standard — a hedge against hyperscalers building their own XPUs outside the NVIDIA stack.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: NVIDIA and MediaTek announced on August 31 that NVIDIA will invest $3.5 billion in MediaTek convertible bonds, and that MediaTek will adopt NVLink Fusion — NVIDIA's newly opened chip-to-chip interconnect standard — as the fabric for the custom AI accelerators it designs for cloud service providers, frontier model labs, and hyperscalers. The bonds convert into MediaTek equity on a future window rather than at signing, and MediaTek shares closed up 10% on the news. NVLink Fusion, together with the just-announced NVHBM memory interface, forms the software-and-silicon suite MediaTek's custom XPUs will plug into.

The mechanism matters more than the dollar figure. NVIDIA's core commercial risk is that every major buyer of its GPUs — Amazon, Google, Microsoft, Meta, OpenAI — is now designing accelerators of its own. NVLink Fusion is NVIDIA's response: instead of losing those customers, it licenses the interconnect that keeps the custom parts inside a data-center topology built around NVIDIA's networking, memory, and software. MediaTek becomes the recommended design partner for that path, and NVIDIA takes a financial position in the outcome.

The broader move fits a pattern of 2026 partnerships in which NVIDIA has traded exclusivity for reach: the OpenAI 10-gigawatt buildout on Vera Rubin systems, the $500 billion financing MOUs with Apollo, Blackstone, BlackRock, Brookfield, Goldman Sachs, and KKR, and now MediaTek. Each locks a segment of the AI supply chain to NVIDIA's stack without requiring the segment to use NVIDIA's own compute silicon.

Takeaway for learners: 'AI infrastructure' is not one company selling one product. It is a stack — chips, memory, interconnect, networking, cooling, software — where the winner is often the layer everyone else has to plug into. Watch which layer a partnership is really about; here it is not GPUs but the wiring between them, and that wiring is what determines whose ecosystem the next decade of AI data centers gets built inside.
